questions.statement: Important business accounts use strong, different passwords or passkeys.
questions.help: Think about email, banking, social media and accounts that store customer information.

questions.statement: Extra sign-in protection is enabled on important accounts wherever available.
questions.help: For example, two-step verification for business email and WhatsApp. Follow the options supported by each app.

questions.statement: Only people who still need access can use our business accounts.
questions.help: Include employees, former helpers, shared logins, social media access and WhatsApp linked devices. For a one-person business, review all connected sessions.

questions.statement: Before releasing goods or services, we confirm digital payments through a trusted bank or payment-provider channel.
questions.help: Do not rely only on a screenshot, SMS alert or message. This includes transfers and payments accepted using POS terminals. Choose “Does not apply” only if your business never accepts digital payments.

questions.statement: Before paying changed supplier bank details, we verify the change using a contact method we already trust.
questions.help: For example, call a known supplier number, not just the number in the message requesting the change. Choose “Does not apply” only if your business never pays suppliers by transfer.

questions.statement: We independently check unexpected requests for money, sign-in codes or links, even when they appear to come from someone familiar.
questions.help: This includes WhatsApp, SMS, email and social media messages.

questions.statement: Work phones and computers lock when they are not being used.
questions.help: Use a PIN, password or biometric lock and avoid leaving a shared business device open.

questions.statement: Business phones, computers and important apps receive security updates.
questions.help: If a device or operating system is no longer supported, there is a plan to move to a supported option.

questions.statement: We use built-in or suitable device protection and install applications from trusted sources.
questions.help: For example, Windows Security, Google Play Protect, verified app stores or other reputable protection appropriate to the device.

questions.statement: We know where important business and customer records are kept and limit unnecessary access.
questions.help: Examples include customer phone numbers, orders, staff details, invoices and delivery addresses.

questions.statement: Important business records have a separate, protected backup copy.
questions.help: The copy should not depend on the same phone or computer that holds the original.

questions.statement: We have checked that an important file or record can be recovered from a backup.
questions.help: A backup is more useful when you know a restore actually works.

questions.statement: Everyone handling business messages or payments knows to pause and report suspicious requests.
questions.help: If you run the business alone, this includes you. Staff do not need technical knowledge to raise a concern.

questions.statement: We know the first actions and official contacts to use after suspected fraud or account compromise.
questions.help: Examples include contacting the bank, mobile operator, account provider or appropriate Nigerian reporting body.

questions.statement: We occasionally review security practices using a realistic example or recent business change.
questions.help: This can be a short discussion about a suspicious WhatsApp message, new worker, lost phone or device replacement.
